report.summary: The model is a generic, bulky red-brick shop rather than a recognizable miniature of the low beige Marathon convenience store. Entry placement is supported, but the massing and signature roadside features need substantial revision.

orientation.summary: The single double principal door is on the -v/SW face. SV4, taken southwest of the building looking ENE, shows the glazed customer frontage with red awnings on this face. SV2 views the -u/SE gable-end and comparatively service-like side, supporting that it is not the entrance face. The labeled -v render and actual inventory agree, with no duplicated principal portal.

issues.problem: The silhouette is wrong: the model has a large near-pyramidal roof and tall, boxy mass, while the references show a low one-story store with mostly low rooflines and a prominent shallow gabled frontage.
issues.fix: Rebuild the roof and elevations as a low convenience-store mass, emphasizing the shallow front gable and subordinate flat/low roof sections visible in SV1–SV4 and the aerial.

issues.problem: The red-brick walls, generic repeated windows and largely blank elevations do not match the beige/tan stucco, cream trim, broad storefront glazing and red awnings that characterize the source.
issues.fix: Use warm beige walls with cream bands, place the broad glazed storefront and red awnings on -v, and simplify the side/rear openings to match the street views.

issues.problem: The miniature omits the Marathon forecourt identity—especially the large white canopy with red/blue fascia and pumps—making the property difficult to recognize.
issues.fix: Add a simplified adjacent fuel canopy, a few blue-and-white pumps and restrained Marathon-colored fascia/signage as the key site-defining accessories.
